inputs.text: Five months after a ceasefire was announced in Gaza, airstrikes are still killing civilians, and the humanitarian situation remains dire. There is little left that connects Palestinians in Gaza with their prewar existence, and the contours of life have become darker and far more brutal, as if the population has been stripped from its past. As 56-year-old Ahmed Baroud, a father of five currently displaced in Deir al-Balah, described it, “Drones never stop buzzing overhead, gunfire and shelling continue almost daily and naval boats fire towards fishermen.”
